title: Do the published numbers still come out of today's code?

what.name: Question
what.value_plain: For 16 published verdicts: has the code behind each one changed since, and does a rerun on today's code give the same numbers?
what.label: OURS

what.name: Reruns
what.value_plain: 10 results rerun on today's code in a sandbox copy; counts must match exactly, returns within 1e-6.
what.label: OURS

how: Git history says which code made each verdict and whether it changed. Each result is rerun and every published number is compared with the new one (3098 numbers compared).
window: DEV only, 2022-04-01 to 2024-06-30 (sealed VALIDATION and HOLDOUT windows were not read)

verdict.label: No verdict flips; mfe_exit does not reproduce, published_strats could not be rerun

why: 9 results reproduce every number exactly (7 had code changes since publishing, none moved a number). The audit text says 8 of 10; its own comparison file shows 9 matching, so the table below is used.
mfe_exit does not reproduce: today's fire files label a different TRAIN window, so the published DEV-only rerun is not repeatable (its 'nothing survives' verdict is untested by it).
published_strats cannot be rerun on this machine because its data folders are absent.
A determinism check (one study run twice) gave identical outputs.

examples.title: Rerun results
examples.caption: mfe_exit return values are withheld in the source (they touched a sealed window by accident); only counts are shown.
